messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Portuguese, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Portuguese line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (locked meaning) | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------------------------|--------------------|------------------------|--------| | Ond' | causal conjunction introducing the reason for the following statement | Por isso | therefore / thus | OK | | io | 1st‑person singular pronoun (subject) – “I” | – (subject omitted) | I | UNNECESSARY | | per | preposition marking benefactive purpose | para | for | OK | | lo | definite article referring to the abstract noun *me'* | o | the | OK | | tuo | 2nd‑person possessive adjective – “your” | teu | your | OK | | me' | abstract noun meaning “the addressee’s highest good” | bem | good | OK | | penso | verb “think” (cognitive) | penso | think | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | e | and | OK | | discerno | verb “judge, deem” (evaluative) | julgo | judge / deem | OK | | che | complementizer introducing a clause – “that” | que | that | OK | | tu | 2nd‑person pronoun (subject) – “you” | – (subject omitted) | you | UNNECESSARY | | mi | 1st‑person object pronoun – “me” | me | me | OK | | segui | verb “follow” (imperative‑like) | segues | follow | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | e | and | OK | | io | 1st‑person pronoun (subject) – “I” | eu | I | OK | | sarò | future copular verb “will be” | serei | will be | OK | | tua | 2nd‑person possessive adjective – “your” | teu | your | OK | | guida | noun “guide” (role) | guia | guide | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | e | and | OK | | trarrotti | future transitive verb “will lead” (directed at addressee) | levarei | will lead | OK | | di | preposition “from” | de | from | OK | | qui | adverb of place “here” | aqui | here | OK | | per | preposition “through” (route/medium) | para | through | OK | | loco | noun “place” (destination) | lugar | place | OK | | etterno | adjective “eternal” (describing the place) | eterno | eternal | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: *io* (line 112) – Portuguese omits the explicit subject. - **UNNECESSARY**: *tu* (line 113) – Portuguese omits the explicit second‑person subject.
All other source words are correctly rendered in the Portuguese translation.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Portuguese script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Portuguese text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
